properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 24 at 11:51PM MDT until October 26 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of north central and west central New Mexico,
including the following areas, in north central New Mexico,
Espanola Valley, Far Northwest Highlands, Jemez Mountains,
Northwest Highlands, Santa Fe Metro Area, Tusas Mountains Including
Chama and Upper Rio Grande Valley. In west central New Mexico, West
Central Highlands.

* WHEN...From Sunday afternoon through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Another round of showers and thunderstorms are expected to impact
areas that have already seen repeated rounds of heavy rainfall.
Rainfall rates in excess of 1 inch per hour will cause rapid
runoff and flash flooding. Those areas recently impacted by heavy
rainfall will be especially susceptible to additional flash
flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 25 at 12:36AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
Elevated fire weather conditions can be expected across portions
of southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi this afternoon.
Relative humidity values are forecast to drop into the 30 to 40
percent range, especially near and north of the Interstate 10 and
12 corridors. The 20 ft wind forecast is expected to remain at or
below 10 mph in most areas, which should limit critical fire
weather conditions or at least the effective spread of fires that
may ignite.

Numerous local burn bans are in place and continue to expand
across LA and MS due to ongoing drought conditions. This now
includes East Feliciana, Iberville, Pointe Coupee, St. Helena, St
Tammany, Tangipahoa, Washington and West Feliciana Parishes along
with Wilkinson, Amite, Pike, and Walthall Counties. Regardless,
outdoor burning is strongly not recommended this afternoon, and
all local restrictions followed.

NWSheadline: ELEVATED FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS TODAY

properties.areaDesc: Majuro Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 25 at 3:01PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Tropical Storm In-fa (30W) is beginning to exit the northern Marshall
Islands as it moves northwest, currently passing near Bikini Atoll.
However, hazardous conditions continue across the region, with
scatterometry this morning showing fresh to strong southwest to west
winds across the northernmost islands and atolls of the RMI. Seas
will remain hazardous to small craft across the area through tonight
as In-fa moves away, due to elevated wind waves and west to
southwest swell, and inter-island travel is strongly discouraged.
Locally heavy showers may produce sudden, strong to near-gale
gusts, leading to locally dangerous conditions. These conditions will
diminish over the next few days as In-fa moves farther away.

For more information on Tropical Storm In-fa, please refer to
bulletins from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header
WTPN31 PGTW and from the National Weather Service under WMO header
WTPQ31 PGUM.

NWSheadline: TROPICAL STORM IN-FA MOVING NORTHWEST, PASSING NEAR BIKINI ATOLL... ...LOCALLY HEAVY SHOWERS, SURGING WEST TO SOUTHWEST WINDS AND SWELL EXPECTED FOR THE NORTHERN RMI

FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has extended
the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Hudspeth County in western Texas...

* Until 1215 AM MDT.

* At 1044 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Acala.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.description:

* WHERE...East Entrance U. S. Waters Strait Of Juan De Fuca.

* WHEN...From 2 AM to 5 PM PDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
properties.instruction:

occurring. Operating a vessel in gale conditions requires

harbor prior to the onset of gale conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 0-20 nm; Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 20-60 nm
properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued October 25 at 12:26AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 0-20 nm...
Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 20-60 nm...

* At 1226 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a strong thunderstorm,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. This strong
thunderstorm was located 45 NM east of Fort Pierce Inlet, moving
west at 20 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Waveland, Nettles Island, Saint Lucie Nuclear Power Plant,
Hutchinson Island South, Sewall's Point, Hobe Sound Wildlife
Refuge, Ocean Breeze Park, Frederick Douglass Park, Hobe Sound
Beach, Walton, Jensen Beach, Port Salerno, Surfside Park, Fort
Pierce Ocean Park, Hobe Sound, Witham Field, Jupiter Island, Rio,
Fort Pierce Inlet and Pepper Beach Park.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, lightning strikes, and heavy downpours. Boaters should seek
safe harbor immediately until this storm passes.

properties.areaDesc: Eddy, NM
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 24 at 10:23PM MDT until October 25 at 1:30AM MDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
FFWMAF

The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Eddy County in southeastern New Mexico...

* Until 130 AM MDT.

* At 1023 PM MDT, A trained weather spotter reported several inches
of standing water from the Charley White Draw over Highway 82 west
of Hope. Flash flooding is ongoing.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Northwestern Eddy County.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
